Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Body, health & movement

vision noun

sight, eyesight

also eyesight, sight (the sense), good eyesight, poor eyesight

classical

Quint. 1.4.20: corpus vīsū tāctūque manifestum (Lewis & Short)
Lucr. 5.101: oculōrum vīsus (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. vision, eyesight

vīsus, vīsūs m.

noun, fourth declension

sight, the faculty of seeing

The sense of sight, and a look or glance; also a thing seen, an apparition (see vision, in a dream).

Other words

  • aciēs oculōrum — keenness of sight, the eyesight

    also used · classical · Caes. B.G. 1.39: nē vultum quidem atque aciem oculōrum ferre potuisse (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. vision, eyesight

    aciēs is an edge, the sharpness of a blade, and so the sharpness of the eyes; also, alone, the eyesight (Lucretius). Its commonest sense is a line of battle (Lewis & Short).

  • aspectus, aspectūs m. — a look, sight; the range of sight

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 7.3.1: prīmō aspectū (Lewis & Short)

    The act of looking and the power of seeing; also the way something looks, its appearance.

Examples

  • corpus vīsū tāctūque manifestum

    a body that sight and touch make plainQuint. 1.4.20 (Lewis & Short)

  • Perspicilla, ut ācrius cernat, quī habet vīsum dēbilem.

    Spectacles, so that someone with weak sight may see more sharply.Comen. OP 79 (perspicillum is a modern word)

See also see, eye, vision.
